description: Savor the iconic taste of India with our Crispy Potato Samosas, a beloved appetizer perfect for any occasion. These golden, flaky pastries are generously filled with a warmly spiced potato and pea mixture, offering a delightful crunch with every bite. Experience the authentic flavors of this classic street food right in your own home.

instructions.title: Prepare the Samosa Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, and carom seeds. Add cold ghee or oil and rub it into the flour with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Gradually add water, kneading until a firm, smooth dough forms. Cover with a damp cloth and let it rest for at least 20 minutes.

instructions.title: Cook the Potato Filling Base
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste, and green chilies, and sauté until the onion turns translucent. Stir in turmeric powder, red chili powder, and coriander powder, cooking for 30 seconds until fragrant.

instructions.title: Combine Filling Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the coarsely mashed potatoes and green peas to the pan. Mix well, ensuring the spices are evenly distributed. Add garam masala, amchur, and salt to taste. Cook for 2-3 minutes, gently mashing some of the potatoes to combine flavors. Remove from heat and stir in fresh chopped coriander leaves. Let the filling cool completely before proceeding.

instructions.title: Shape the Samosa Pockets
instructions.text: Divide the rested dough into 8-10 equal portions. Roll each portion into an oval shape, about 6-7 inches long and 3-4 inches wide. Cut each oval in half lengthwise, creating two semi-circles. Lightly moisten the straight edge of each semi-circle with water.

instructions.title: Fill and Seal the Samosas
instructions.text: Take one semi-circle, bring the straight edges together to form a cone shape, pressing firmly to seal the seam. Hold the cone in one hand and spoon 1-2 tablespoons of the cooled potato filling inside. Moisten the top edges of the cone with water. Press the edges together to seal the samosa, creating a triangular or pyramidal shape. Ensure the seal is tight to prevent filling from escaping during frying. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

instructions.title: Fry the Crispy Samosas
instructions.text: Heat vegetable oil in a deep kadai or heavy-bottomed pan over medium-low heat. The oil should be hot enough to sizzle but not smoke. Carefully slide a few samosas into the hot oil, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Fry on medium-low heat, turning occasionally, for 10-15 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy on all sides. This slow frying ensures the pastry cooks through and becomes flaky. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain excess oil on paper towels. Serve hot with chutney.

tips: For the crispiest samosa crust, ensure your dough is firm and kneaded well, and always fry on medium-low heat. Too high heat will brown them quickly without cooking the crust through.
To prevent your samosas from bursting, ensure the filling is completely cooled before use and seal the edges tightly with a little water. You can also crimp the edges with a fork for extra security.

Samosas can be prepared ahead of time and frozen before frying. Arrange them on a baking sheet until solid, then transfer to a freezer bag. Fry directly from frozen, adding a few extra minutes to the cooking time.
